column3: Therefore, putting away all malice and all deceit and hypocrisies and envies and all slanders,
like newborn infants, long for the pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow into salvation,
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good.
Coming to him, a living stone rejected by people but chosen and precious before God,
you yourselves also, as living stones, are being built into a spiritual house for a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For it stands in Scripture: “Look, I lay in Zion a chosen and precious cornerstone, and the one who believes in him will certainly not be put to shame.”
Therefore the honor is for you who believe, but for those who disbelieve, “the stone that the builders rejected—this one became the head of the corner,”
and “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble because they disobey the word, to which they also were appointed.

But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s possession, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
Beloved, I urge you as foreigners and sojourners to abstain from fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul.
Keep your conduct among the Gentiles honorable, so that in the matter in which they speak against you as evildoers, by observing your good works they may glorify God on the day of visitation.
Submit to every human institution for the Lord’s sake, whether to a king as supreme,
or to governors as sent by him for punishment of evildoers and praise of those who do good.
For this is the will of God: by doing good to silence the ignorance of foolish people,
as free people, yet not using freedom as a covering for evil, but as servants of God.
Honor everyone. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king.
Household servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle but also to the crooked.
For this is gracious if, because of consciousness of God, someone endures sorrows while suffering unjustly.
For what credit is there if, when you sin and are beaten, you endure it? But if when doing good and suffering you endure, this is gracious before God.
For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example so that you might follow in his footsteps.
“He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth.”
When insulted, he did not insult in return; when suffering, he did not threaten, but entrusted himself to the one who judges justly.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, so that having died to sins we might live to righteousness. By his wound you were healed.
For you were like sheep going astray, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
